links.outcome: Female and non-White surgeon representation in AI-generated images versus real-world demographics
links.effect: Midjourney and Stable Diffusion depicted female surgeons at 0% and 1.8% and non-White surgeons at 0.5% and 0.6% (P < .001); DALL-E 2 matched attendings (15.9% vs 14.7% female) but underestimated trainees.
links.quote: In contrast, Midjourney and Stable Diffusion had significantly lower representation of images of female (0% and 1.8%, respectively; P < .001) and non-White (0.5% and 0.6%, respectively; P < .001) surgeons than DALL-E 2 or true demographic data.

links.outcome: Model output demographic representation compared with real-world attending surgeon and trainee demographics
links.effect: Two of three models depicted over 98% of surgeons as White and male; all 3 models underestimated trainee representation (DALL-E 2 female 15.9% vs 35.8%, P < .001).
links.quote: In this study, 2 leading publicly available text-to-image generators amplified societal biases, depicting over 98% surgeons as White and male.

unlisted_practices: Geographic-based prompting to alter demographic representation in text-to-image outputs

screen.reason: Empirically evaluates demographic representation and bias (race and gender) of AI text-to-image generators depicting surgical specialties compared against real-world physician workforce benchmarks.
